northStar: VS Code familiarity + Cursor-class AI coding + Replit-class general assistance + JetBrains-class semantic intelligence + Zed-class responsiveness + Cortex system-level understanding and verification

competitors.name: VS Code
weaknesses: extension authority remains broad once installed
extension performance and configuration burden can accumulate

competitors.name: Cursor
weaknesses: approval fatigue remains a documented agent problem
editor foundation inherits VS Code lineage

competitors.name: JetBrains
weaknesses: heavy project analysis can increase startup/resource cost
semantic depth is tightly coupled to IDE/language implementations

competitors.name: Zed
weaknesses: language/debug tooling often depends on external binaries
structurallyEliminate: manual external-tool friction where safe acquisition is possible

competitors.name: Replit
strengths: general assistance spanning code and environment
weaknesses: local-first professional IDE depth is not its core architecture

innovations.purpose: Deliver a familiar professional workbench without inheriting an Electron/VS Code runtime as Cortex core architecture.
innovations.mechanism: Tauri desktop shell, system WebView, Monaco editing surface, Rust native workspace/protocol/security/terminal services, and isolated child services.
innovations.expectedAdvantage: Lower idle memory and package overhead, stronger native service boundaries, and freedom to evolve internals independently of VS Code.
innovations.tradeoff: WebView behavior varies by platform and some Node-first integrations require adapters.
innovations.failureMode: Cross-platform WebView or native integration divergence causes reliability regressions that erase the efficiency advantage.
innovations.measurementMethod: Compare cold start, warm start, idle RSS, active RSS, package size, crash rate, editor latency and terminal latency against Electron baseline and leading IDEs.
innovations.fallback: Maintain a benchmarked Electron reference shell and switch only if reliability/productivity wins outweigh measured resource penalties.
innovations.validationExperiment: Run identical 10K/100K/1M-file workspaces on Linux, Windows and macOS with clean profiles and record startup, memory, latency, crash and packaging metrics.

scale.1x: Single repository and normal local tooling.
scale.10x: Large monorepo with several language services and terminals.
scale.100x: Million-file workspace, many concurrent services and long-lived session; enforce degradation budgets instead of global collapse.

innovations.purpose: Give Cortex one evidence-linked engineering model spanning source through production behavior.
innovations.mechanism: Rebuildable graph joins symbols, files, dependencies, tests, schemas, runtime evidence, Git, infrastructure, deployments, ownership and agent changes.
innovations.expectedAdvantage: Higher impact-analysis accuracy and less repeated context gathering than file/vector-only assistants.
innovations.tradeoff: Graph ingestion and freshness consume compute, storage and implementation complexity.
innovations.failureMode: Stale or poisoned graph state causes confident but incorrect impact analysis.
innovations.measurementMethod: Measure retrieval precision/recall, freshness lag, rebuild time, incremental update latency, graph storage cost and correct-impact prediction rate.
innovations.fallback: Mark stale partitions unavailable and fall back to direct repository/runtime queries until rebuilt.
innovations.validationExperiment: Inject branch changes, generated files, schema migrations and runtime changes into benchmark repositories and compare graph answers with repository ground truth.

scale.100x: Many services and millions of graph edges; partition, compact and rebuild derived regions independently.

innovations.purpose: Prevent AI agents and extensions from receiving ambient machine or production authority.
innovations.mechanism: Deny-by-default capabilities plus execution levels from OBSERVE through PRODUCTION, enforced at policy and process/sandbox boundaries with audit evidence.
innovations.expectedAdvantage: Safer autonomy with deterministic authority boundaries and fewer meaningless approval prompts.
innovations.tradeoff: Strict boundaries can break tools that assume unrestricted filesystem/network/process access.
innovations.failureMode: Policy says denied while an underlying process boundary still permits the action.
innovations.measurementMethod: Run adversarial filesystem, symlink, process-tree, network, secret, Git, database and deployment escape tests; record denied-action correctness and false-positive rate.
innovations.fallback: Quarantine the execution class and require explicit developer-controlled external execution until containment is restored.
innovations.validationExperiment: Execute a maintained malicious-tool corpus across every execution level and OS and require zero boundary escapes before qualification.

scale.100x: High-concurrency automation; authority must remain per-principal with no shared-capability leakage.

innovations.purpose: Keep VS Code ecosystem strengths without inheriting ambient authority, startup drag, failure coupling and opaque resource cost.
innovations.mechanism: Signed packages, capability manifests, lazy activation, isolated hosts, transactional install/rollback, health accounting, quarantine and compatibility adapters.
innovations.expectedAdvantage: Broad extensibility with attributable cost and local failure containment.
innovations.tradeoff: Not every VS Code extension can be supported unchanged; compatibility requires measured adapters.
innovations.failureMode: Compatibility pressure gradually recreates unrestricted Node authority and shared-host coupling.
innovations.measurementMethod: Measure extension compatibility corpus pass rate, activation latency, per-extension RSS/CPU/I/O, crash containment and permission enforcement.
innovations.fallback: Run unsupported extensions in an explicitly isolated compatibility tier or refuse installation with a precise unsupported-capability report.
innovations.validationExperiment: Qualify a representative corpus of popular language, formatter, debugger, Git, theme and tooling extensions under failure, hang and malicious-behavior injection.

scale.100x: Marketplace-scale catalog; metadata/index operations must not load extension code.

innovations.purpose: Make AI capability independent from any single model vendor while preserving task quality and cost control.
innovations.mechanism: Provider-neutral request contract, provider adapters, policy routing, budgets, retries, circuit breakers, usage accounting and local/custom provider support.
innovations.expectedAdvantage: Reduced vendor lock-in, graceful provider failure and task-specific quality/cost routing.
innovations.tradeoff: Lowest-common-denominator abstractions can hide provider-specific strengths if adapters are too generic.
innovations.failureMode: Provider drift or adapter mismatch silently degrades tool behavior or reasoning quality.
innovations.measurementMethod: Track task success, latency, cost, token use, tool-call correctness, schema conformance and failover time per provider/model.
innovations.fallback: Route to last-known-qualified provider/model profile or local-only operation while preserving non-AI IDE functions.
innovations.validationExperiment: Replay the same engineering task suite against multiple providers plus injected timeout/rate-limit/malformed-output faults and compare outcomes.

scale.1x: Single developer with one or two providers.
scale.10x: Team workloads with concurrent routing and budgets.
scale.100x: Large commercial fleet; cost, rate limits and provider incidents must degrade selectively rather than globally.

innovations.purpose: Remove artificial Ask/Plan/Agent/Debug mode selection while still choosing the right engineering depth and authority.
innovations.mechanism: Classify developer intent, gather graph/memory/runtime context, infer assistance depth, compose specialized agents/tools, then gate side effects by security policy.
innovations.expectedAdvantage: Fewer interaction steps and context switches without sacrificing reviewability or safety.
innovations.tradeoff: Misclassification can invoke too much or too little machinery.
innovations.failureMode: A simple request becomes expensive/slow, or a complex/risky request is under-planned.
innovations.measurementMethod: Measure task completion, routing accuracy, unnecessary tool invocations, developer corrections, time-to-correct-change and approval count.
innovations.fallback: Expose the inferred plan/depth for correction and allow deterministic developer override without requiring persistent mode switching.
innovations.validationExperiment: Replay a labeled corpus from explanation through production deployment and compare inferred depth/authority with expert classification.

scale.10x: Multi-file objectives and several specialized agents.
scale.100x: Large task graphs; scheduler must bound parallelism, cost and authority while preserving deterministic evidence lineage.

innovations.purpose: Keep models from becoming the system of record or silently declaring work correct.
innovations.mechanism: Models propose actions and claims; repository state, System Graph, tests, runtime evidence, policy decisions and durable ledgers authorize and verify outcomes.
innovations.expectedAdvantage: Higher correctness, reproducibility and auditability than model-confidence-driven workflows.
innovations.tradeoff: Verification adds latency and compute to changes.
innovations.failureMode: Weak or incomplete verification evidence is mistaken for proof.
innovations.measurementMethod: Track escaped regressions, false completion claims, evidence coverage, replay determinism and verification latency.
innovations.fallback: Downgrade status to unverified and require developer review rather than asserting completion.
innovations.validationExperiment: Seed tasks with misleading model-friendly cues and require Cortex to reject completion whenever tests/runtime/policy evidence contradicts the model output.

scale.100x: Large agent graphs; evidence must remain attributable, compactable and replayable without trusting agent summaries.

innovations.purpose: Keep editor state and developer work alive when individual services, extensions, models, terminals or indexes fail.
innovations.mechanism: Process/service isolation, restartable derived services, session journal, unsaved-buffer recovery, transactional AI edits, update/extension rollback and rebuildable indexes.
innovations.expectedAdvantage: Lower blast radius and faster recovery than monolithic failure coupling.
innovations.tradeoff: More process boundaries and recovery protocols increase orchestration complexity.
innovations.failureMode: Shared hidden state makes a supposedly local restart corrupt or desynchronize another subsystem.
innovations.measurementMethod: Fault-inject crashes/hangs/corruption and measure data loss, workbench survival, recovery time and state consistency.
innovations.fallback: Disable the failed subsystem, preserve editor/workspace state and offer explicit rebuild/restart/rollback without forcing full application loss.
innovations.validationExperiment: Continuously kill LSP, terminal, extension, model, index and updater processes during active work and verify session integrity plus independent recovery.

scale.10x: Several concurrent failures during active editing.
scale.100x: Fleet/provider incident; recovery must avoid synchronized restart storms and preserve local work.

qualificationRule: An architectural claim may be called superior only when the relevant benchmark has current comparative evidence. Missing evidence means unqualified, not assumed superior.
